case.question: How can I connect with my newborn during feeding?
case.expected_behaviour: Gentle age-suitable interaction, without feeding-treatment advice.

retrieved.text: COMMUNICATE Look into baby’s eyes and talk to your baby. When you are breastfeeding is a good time. Even a newborn baby sees your face and hears your voice.
retrieved.title: birth up to 1 week: communication
retrieved.source_title: Care for Child Development: Counselling Cards

retrieved.text: 2. Let baby know mummy! • Face baby, and smile, see if he smiles back • Open and close your mouth making a soft sound. See if baby looks at your mouth. • Hold baby’s hands and gently move them over your face. Let baby hold your nose. Chat with baby • Talk to baby all the time – during changing, feeding and bath time • Describe what you are doing • Talk about what baby is doing • Soon baby will know your voice!
retrieved.title: 2. Let baby know mummy

retrieved.text: BREASTFEEDING Newborn upto 1 week • Immediately after birth, put the baby on skin-to-skin contact with the mother for at least one hour. • Initiate breastfeeding within the first hour after birth. Give your baby colostrum (the first yellowish, clear, whitish milk). It protects the baby from many illnesses. • Breastfeed on demand (day and night, as often as the baby wants) at least 8 times in 24 hours. Frequent feeding produces more milk. • If the baby is small (low birth weight - <2500g), feed at least every 2 to 3 hours. Wake the baby for feeding after 3 hours, if baby does not wake self. • DO NOT give other foods. Breast milk is all your baby needs.
retrieved.title: Breastfeeding: newborn up to 1 week

answer:
Feeding time is a wonderful opportunity to connect with your newborn. Here are simple ways to bond:

* Look into your baby's eyes and talk to them while you feed.
* Chat with your baby and describe what you are doing.
* Let your baby hear your voice so they will soon learn to recognize it.
